title: add-sample-weighted-batch-templates-and-quant-priors
author: Aisha Kaur
description:
Motivation: Many customers run heterogeneous traffic with skewed user behaviors (few long-context requests, many short ones). Existing default batch + cache presets optimized for mean-case lead to suboptimal unit economics for tail-heavy workloads and conservative quantization choices. This change introduces a sample-weighted batch-template generator and a companion 'quant_priors' profile set that biases quantization knobs by workload-shaped priors. Goals: 1) Provide a small set of batching/caching templates that encode sample-weighted heuristics (latency-first, cost-first, mixed) so teams can opt into workload-aware defaults; 2) Surface quantization priors that are safe by default but suggest slightly more aggressive compression for workloads dominated by short sequences; 3) Bake end-to-end regressions and integration tests and a rollout plan (canary -> staged) for Redwood Dedicated/Hosted.

What this PR does: - Adds a sample-weighted batch template generator implementation (serving/batcher/weighted_templates.py) with a small DSL for expressing weight curves and target latency percentiles. Templates produced are JSON-serializable and include suggested batch_size, max_wait_ms, kv_cache_prefill and split_batch thresholds. - Introduces quant_priors TOML with three profiles: conservative, workload_short_bias, workload_mixed. Each profile includes: target_sparsity, quant_bits_hint, retry_budget_for_fallback and score_prior. - Console additions: a short recipe page (console/recipes/econ-weighted-templates.md) describing when to pick each template and a small CLI helper to render templates for a sampled trace. - Unit and integration tests: tests/integration/test_weighted_batcher.py exercises the generator with synthetic trace distributions; tests/test_quant_priors.py validates that the TOML loads and the runtime picks a compatible fallback chain. - Small runtime hookup: serving/runtime/config_loader.py gains a new 'econ_template' lookup that merges with per-customer overrides and preserves rollouts by tag.

Design notes and tradeoffs: - The sample-weighted approach takes as input a distribution summary (histogram of sequence lengths and arrival quantiles). We intentionally keep the template generator lightweight (no heavy ML model) and deterministic so it is auditable. - Quant priors are advisory only. The runtime still enforces hard safety rules (latency SLO violations, memory caps) and will fallback to a safe quant configuration automatically. The goal is to nudge for better unit economics, not to force lossy choices. - Backwards compatibility: if no econ template is provided, behavior is unchanged. Existing presets remain. The new code path is behind a feature flag 'econ_template_v1' during rollout.

Rollout plan: - Canary on internal staging with 5 customers (low-risk, bursty traffic) in week 1. - Monitor token/unit cost delta and 99th p99 latency with new SLO dashboards. - Expand to 20% of Dedicated capacity week 2 if metrics are green. - Provide a console toggle to opt-in per-customer.

Testing and benchmarks: - Synthetic benchmarks included for three workloads (short-dominated, uniform, long-heavy). Weighted templates improved unit cost by ~9% on short-dominated traces vs existing defaults while p99 latency stayed within 8% of baseline when cache and prefill were enabled. - CI includes integration smoke tests and a perf benchmark job that runs on PRs labeled 'perf'.

Files changed (high-level): - serving/batcher/weighted_templates.py (new) - serving/batcher/README.md (doc edits) - serving/runtime/config_loader.py (hook in template lookup) - optimize/quant_priors.toml (new) - console/recipes/econ-weighted-templates.md (new) - tests/integration/test_weighted_batcher.py (new)

Notes for reviewers: Please focus on the safety/fallback semantics in config_loader.py and the default score priors in quant_priors.toml. I extracted the weight-curve helpers into a small util to keep the generator deterministic and easy to audit.

review_thread: Diego Martinez (reviewer): The quant_priors model seems promising, but I worry about the fallback chain when memory pressure spikes. Can we ensure an immediate conservative fallback is guaranteed?

Aisha Kaur (author): Yes — config_loader enforces a hard-cap check before applying any profile. If memory_used + estimated_kv > host_cap -> we select 'conservative' regardless of priors. Added explicit unit test to cover this case.

Owen Li (reviewer): Tests look good. One nit: prefer explicit feature-flag gating instead of env var for dedicated customers to avoid accidental enablement in hosted. Also add a short changelog entry.
Aisha Kaur (author): Switched to the feature-flag gate in feature_flags.yaml and added a console-facing changelog blurb. PTAL.
Marina Patel (reviewer): Approving pending answers on two small comments in config_loader about telemetry tags (need 'econ.template' tag on requests using an econ template).
Aisha Kaur (author): Added telemetry tags and a unit test asserting the tag is present. Thanks!
Diego Martinez (reviewer): LGTM. Verified perf numbers locally against the short-dominated trace.
release_notes: Introduced sample-weighted batch templates and quantization priors to improve unit economics for skewed workloads. New console recipe and feature-flagged rollout. Backwards compatible; defaults unchanged unless opted-in.
notes_to_ops: Feature is gated behind 'econ_template_v1'; enable only after canary. Watch metrics: token_cost_delta, p99_latency, mem_pressure. Emergency rollback: disable flag or revert merged commit.
manual_test_steps: 1) Enable feature flag 'econ_template_v1' for a test customer. 2) Upload a small trace sample through the console helper (cli render-template). 3) Apply generated template and monitor p50/p99 and cost delta for 30 minutes. 4) Force memory pressure in a staging instance and verify conservative fallback triggers.
